headings.title: Annual commissioner reports on administrative procedure law
headings.reviewNote: Requires each administrative hearing commissioner serving on August 13, 1984, to submit an annual report to the governor suggesting administrative procedure law improvements until expiration of the term served on that date.

headings.title: Additional compensation for subsection 1 reporting duties
headings.reviewNote: Sets compensation for subsection 1 duties so that total compensation equals the combined compensation under sections 621.015 and 621.055, paid in the same manner as other compensation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 621.017; added August 13, 1984 term-limitation scope in subsection 1 and statutory compensation formula in subsection 2.

headings.title: Commission jurisdiction over enumerated licensing agency cases
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to conduct hearings and make findings of fact and conclusions of law in license revocation, suspension, probation, examination-refusal, or issuance/renewal-refusal cases for nineteen enumerated state agencies and boards.

headings.title: Automatic inclusion of newly created licensing agencies
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any future statutorily created administrative agency with power to issue, revoke, suspend, or place a license on probation to this law.

headings.title: Jurisdiction over unlicensed design-profession cases under section 327.076
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to conduct hearings and issue findings and conclusions in cases brought by the architects, engineers, land surveyors, landscape architects, and licensed interior designers board against unlicensed persons under section 327.076.

headings.title: Prehearing settlement offer and disclosure duties after August 28, 1995
headings.reviewNote: Requires subsection 1 or 2 agencies after August 28, 1995, to provide licensees a written violation description, cited laws/rules, supporting documents, and initial settlement offer (or file a contested case), allow sixty days to consider, advise of fifteen-day commission review option, and advise unrepresented licensees of right to counsel.

headings.title: Licensee rescission right and finality of submitted settlements
headings.reviewNote: Allows a licensee requesting commission review under subsection 4(3) to rescind and withdraw from the settlement prior to finality (rendering admissions inadmissible), and provides that a submitted settlement is not final until the commission enters findings and conclusions.

headings.title: Default decisions for failure to respond and motion to set aside
headings.reviewNote: Mandates entry of a default decision without further proceedings when a division of professional registration licensee fails to plead or respond after adequate notice under sections 536.067 and 621.100, and provides that a default decision may be set aside on motion within thirty days showing a meritorious defense and good cause.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections of 621.045 (including 2026 S.B. 1233); refined subsections 4-6 to capture the August 28, 1995 date, settlement rescission/finality rules, and 30-day motion to set aside default decisions.

headings.title: Right to appeal gaming commission decisions within thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Grants a right to appeal Missouri gaming commission findings, decisions, or determinations under section 313.917 by filing a petition within thirty days of mailing or delivery (whichever is earlier), and prescribes required notice of appeal language.

headings.title: Chapter 536 hearing procedures and binding decisions
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 536 procedures to hearings and determinations and makes commission decisions binding subject to appeal by either party.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 621.047; added section 313.917 reference, 30-day filing deadline, and prescribed appeal notice in subsection 1.

headings.title: Appeals from director of revenue decisions within thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Grants a right to appeal any finding, order, decision, assessment, or additional assessment of the director of revenue by filing a petition within thirty days of mailing or delivery (whichever is earlier), and prescribes required appeal-notice language.

headings.title: Hearing procedures, six-percent interest, and burden of proof
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 536 procedures (permitting rules-of-evidence proof of chapter 144 exemptions), requires transcripts at reasonable cost, makes decisions binding subject to appeal, awards 6% interest to prevailing taxpayers (except section 144.700 protested taxes), and places the burden of proof on the taxpayer except for fraud, transferee liability, and specified post-protest deficiency increases.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 621.050; corrected filing deadline in subsection 1 from fabricated 60 days to 30 days and detailed all three director-of-revenue burden-of-proof exceptions and 6% interest rule in subsection 2.

headings.title: Appeals from tax credit, abatement, or loan decisions within thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Grants a right to appeal agency eligibility decisions on state-administered or subsidized tax credits, abatements, or loans under section 285.025(1) within thirty days of mailing or delivery (whichever is earlier), and prescribes required appeal-notice language.

headings.title: Chapter 536 hearing procedures and binding decisions
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 536 procedures to hearings and determinations and makes commission decisions binding subject to appeal by either party.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 621.052; corrected filing deadline in subsection 1 from fabricated 60 days to 30 days and replaced misplaced notice heading in subsection 2 with chapter 536 procedures and binding effect.

headings.title: Medical assistance provider review, interest, and burden of proof
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes section 208.153 medical assistance providers to seek commission review of specified department of social services actions under section 208.156(2)-(5) using chapter 536 procedures, requires transcripts, makes decisions binding subject to appeal, allows 8% interest to prevailing providers, and places the burden of proof on the provider.

headings.title: Additional annual compensation for commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Grants each commissioner $5,000 annually plus any section 105.005 salary adjustment for additional duties under this section and section 208.156.

headings.title: Required notice of appeal rights and small-claim accumulation
headings.reviewNote: Requires appealable department of social services decisions to include prescribed appeal-notice language reflecting the thirty-day deadline, with an exception allowing claims under $500 to be accumulated to $500 and filed within ninety days.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 621.055; added 8% interest and provider burden of proof in subsection 1, $5,000 annual compensation in subsection 2, and the $500/90-day small-claim accumulation exception in subsection 3.

headings.title: Regular merit employee right of appeal within thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Grants regular employees (section 36.020) dismissed, involuntarily demoted for cause, or suspended over five working days the right to appeal within thirty days of the action's effective date, and prescribes required appeal-notice language.

headings.title: Hearing procedures, nonpublic hearings, and reinstatement or dismissal orders
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 536 procedures, authorizes stipulated/consent/summary/default dispositions, keeps hearings nonpublic unless requested by the employee, requires transcripts, makes decisions binding subject to appeal, and authorizes ordering reinstatement or sustaining dismissal.

headings.title: Separate post-finality action for reinstatement date and back pay
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission, after a reinstatement order becomes final and affirmed, to commence a separate action (by hearing, affidavit, depositions, stipulations, or agreement, nonpublic unless requested by the employee) to determine the reinstatement date and back pay owed.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 621.075; realigned shifted headings across subsections 1-3, removed fabricated involuntary-transfer scope in subsection 1, and captured the separate back-pay action in subsection 3.

headings.title: Service of complaints, publication notice, and agency intervention
headings.reviewNote: Requires serving agency or attorney general complaints and hearing notices on licensees personally, by abode service, certified mail, or section 506.160(3) publication, requires notifying the issuing agency of attorney general complaints, and provides that the agency may intervene and retain legal counsel.

headings.title: Default decisions for failure to respond and motion to set aside
headings.reviewNote: Mandates entry of a default decision without further proceedings when a division of professional registration licensee fails to plead or respond after adequate notice under this section and section 536.067, and provides that a default decision may be set aside on motion within thirty days showing a meritorious defense and good cause.

headings.title: Agency custodian sworn affidavit regarding license status
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an agency records custodian may submit a sworn affidavit stating six enumerated license-status facts, received as substantial and competent evidence creating a rebuttable presumption, subject to section 536.070 when license status is a material fact in issue.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 621.100; moved agency intervention/counsel to subsection 1, default decisions to subsection 2, and isolated license-status affidavits in subsection 3.

headings.title: Filing date for registered, certified, or other delivery methods
headings.reviewNote: Deems documents sent by registered or certified mail filed on the post office mailing date, and documents sent by any other method filed on the date received by the commission.

headings.title: Extension of deadlines falling on weekends or legal holidays
headings.reviewNote: Makes performance of any act timely on the next succeeding non-weekend, non-holiday day when the last prescribed day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or state legal holiday.

headings.title: Discretionary regulation for electronic facsimile filing
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the administrative hearing commission may by regulation provide for filing documents by electronic facsimile transmission.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 621.205; combined mail and non-mail delivery rules in subsection 1, replaced inaccurate subsection 2 with weekend/holiday deadline extension, and preserved permissive facsimile rulemaking in subsection 3.

headings.title: Transfer of environmental contested case appeals and final decision authority
headings.reviewNote: Transfers contested case appeal authority under chapters 236, 256, 260, 444, 640, 643, and 644 and five listed environmental commissions to the AHC, retains final decision authority with those commissions except for chapter 236, chapter 256, section 260.235, and section 260.249 appeals (where AHC renders final decisions), and permits stipulated/summary/default dispositions.

headings.title: Thirty-day appeal deadline and hearing or decision timelines
headings.reviewNote: Allows filing a notice of appeal within thirty days of mailing or delivery (whichever is earlier), provides AHC may hold hearings within ninety days and shall issue a recommended or final decision within 120 days, with timelines extendable at the permittee's sole discretion.

headings.title: Appeal notice language, record transmittal, and commission final decisions
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes appeal-notice text for department of natural resources decisions, requires fifteen-day transmittal of the record and transcript with the recommended decision, sets a 180-day final decision deadline (extendable at permittee's sole discretion), and allows adopting, modifying, or vacating only with written specific reasons.

headings.title: Interest on wrongfully collected or erroneously paid amounts
headings.reviewNote: Allows interest at the section 32.065 director of revenue rate on wrongfully collected or erroneously paid amounts if the appealing person prevails.

headings.title: Appropriations from department of natural resources funds
headings.reviewNote: Requires appropriations from respective department of natural resources funds to cover the commission's costs associated with these appeals.

headings.title: Burden of proof and chapter 536 hearing procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires the burden of proof in section 621.250 hearings to comply with section 640.012 and hearings to follow chapter 536 and its regulations.

headings.title: Exhaustion of administrative remedies prerequisite to court action
headings.reviewNote: Bars any court cause of action or appeal arising from a subsection 1 commission finding, order, decision, or assessment unless the party filed a notice of appeal and received a final decision under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 621.250; corrected count of listed commissions (five, not six) in subsection 1 and replaced shifted and fabricated headings in subsections 3-7 (interest, DNR fund appropriations, burden of proof, and exhaustion).

headings.title: Initial ten-hour special education training and website posting
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least three commissioners to complete at least ten hours of initial special education training (selected with DESE and Missouri's IDEA parent training center) as the sole commissioners assigned to due process hearings, with materials posted online within ten business days if provider policies allow.

headings.title: Annual five-hour continuing special education training and posting
headings.reviewNote: Requires each assigned commissioner to complete at least five hours of annual training selected with DESE and the IDEA parent training center, with materials posted online within ten business days if provider rules allow.

headings.title: Direct posting duty for DESE and parent training center sessions
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE, the IDEA-funded parent training and information center, or a provider working directly on their behalf to post training materials, audio, and video on its own website within ten business days when providing training directly.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 621.253; added the three-commissioner/10-hour threshold, IDEA parent training center consultation, and provider-policy conditions.

headings.title: Establishment and dedicated use of educational due process fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Administrative Hearing Commission Educational Due Process Hearing Fund in the state treasury, administered by the commission with the state treasurer as custodian, used solely for commission expenditures attributable to due process hearings and related state and federal laws.

headings.title: Nonreversion of remaining fund balances
headings.reviewNote: Exempts moneys remaining in the fund at the end of the biennium from reversion to general revenue under section 33.080.

headings.title: State treasurer investment and interest credit
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state treasurer to invest fund moneys in the same manner as other funds and credit all earned interest and moneys to the fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 621.255; verified alignment with archived source text.

headings.title: Right to appeal crime victims' compensation decisions
headings.reviewNote: Grants any person the right to appeal a department of public safety decision under section 595.036 regarding a crime victims' compensation claim under sections 595.010 to 595.075.

headings.title: Thirty-day filing deadline and required appeal notice
headings.reviewNote: Entitles appellants to a hearing upon filing a petition within thirty days of mailing or delivery of the director's decision (whichever is earlier), and prescribes appeal-notice text for the director's decision.

headings.title: Binding decisions and chapter 536 hearing procedures
headings.reviewNote: Makes commission decisions binding subject to appeal by either party and applies chapter 536 procedures to hearings and determinations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 621.275; verified alignment with archived source text.
